title: Contract Capacity Synchronization Planner - Aug 2027
body:
Purpose:
This is a working planner for synchronizing per-contract Dedicated GPU reservations across regions and time windows to reduce fragmentation and improve utilization while preserving contractual SLAs. The aim is not to replace contract entitlements but to provide an operational mapping and algorithmic recommendation that SRE/Capacity can apply during onboarding and quarterly review cycles.

Context / motivation:
- Over the last 6 quarters we see increased tail fragmentation: many mid-sized commitments (8–64 GPUs) with narrow peak windows in different regions creates low-util islands.
- Customers increasingly request region affinity + predictable latency. We must honor region pins while improving global utilization through time-window alignment and coordinated auto-burst policies.
- This doc proposes a synchronization planner (heuristic + scoring) and an exportable per-contract allocation sheet for onboarding and renewal conversations.

Key terminology (quick):
- Committed-GPUs: contractual baseline guaranteed to customer (billing/guarantee).
- Burst-Pool: ephemeral additional capacity usable if free; not guaranteed.
- Peak-window: customer defined daily time window where usage typically spikes (local timezone).
- Synchronization score: composite metric (0-100) used to rank how well a contract's window/region fits with neighbors.

High level approach:
1) Ingest commitments (contract id, committed gpus, preferred region(s), preferred instance family, peak window local, timezone).
2) Normalize windows to UTC and compute overlap density per region by hour-of-day.
3) Compute a candidate reslice where we adjust assigned GPU distribution across multiple region sites (when contract allows soft-region affinity) and/or shift optional burst eligibility windows to maximize per-region hourly utilization subject to SLA blackout periods.
4) Score proposals by: SLA-risk, customer-preferences penalty, projected utilization delta, and ops friction cost.
5) Produce a per-contract allocation record with: baseline assignment, suggested burst-cap eligibility, synchronized window(s), and migration/rollback notes.

Sample per-contract allocation exports (human-readable; produced by planner):

Contract table (example rows):
ContractID | Customer | Region_pref | Committed_GPUs | Preferred_Type | Peak_window_UTC | Runway_months | Sync_suggestion | Notes
C-4521 | AtlasHealth | us-west1 | 24 | A100-80GB | 21:00-03:00 | 12 | Keep baseline + allow burst in us-central for 02:00-04:00 | Low-risk, can stretch to central for overflow (data residency flagged)
C-4789 | FinBox | eu-west1 | 40 | H100 | 11:00-15:00 | 24 | Shift 6 GPUs to staggered window 13:00-17:00; qualify for cross-region burst | Negotiated optional cross-region allowance in contract addendum
C-5033 | RetailCore | ap-northeast1 | 8 | A100-40GB | 00:00-08:00 | 6 | Consolidate with C-5019 into pooled tranche (same SLA) | Temporary pooling recommended for Q3 ramp

Operational heuristics / formulas used in scoring:
- HourlyOverlap(region r, window w) = sum_over_contracts_in_r 1_{contract_window includes hour}
- SynchronizationScore = 40*UtilGainNormalized + 30*(1 - SLA_RiskNormalized) + 20*OpsCostNormalized + 10*PrefMatchNormalized
- UtilGainNormalized = min(1, (projected_util_after - current_util)/0.25)  // 25ppt improvement cap
- SLA_RiskNormalized = risk_metric scaled 0..1 (higher is worse), derived from: regional failover latency, data residency constraints, contractual blackout windows

Small worked example (region us-west1):
- Baseline committed: 720 GPUs across 18 contracts. Hourly profile shows two peaks: 19:00-22:00 UTC (local business spikes) and 02:00-03:00 UTC (overlap from APAC).
- Proposed sync: encourage 6 small contracts to shift optional non-critical batch windows from 19:00 to 02:00 (2-hour shift).
- Projected outcome: peak-to-trough variance reduces from 38% to 20%, freeing ~86 GPUs of effective capacity during primetime for on-demand / burst usage.

Guidelines for applying recommendations to contracts:
- If contract explicitly forbids region movement, only suggest burst eligibility or cross-region overflow with explicit consent.
- For customers with short runway (<9 months) prefer non-invasive suggestions (burst only).
- Prioritize edits for contracts whose SyncScore > 55 and where UtilGainNormalized > 0.10.
- Always generate a rollback plan: which workloads to move back and timing windows.

Communication templates (snippets to include in renewal/onboarding emails):
- Brief: "We recommend a minor window alignment and optional cross-region burst to lower your unit cost and improve availability. No guaranteed changes are made without approval. See proposed schedule attached."
- Technical: attach per-contract minute-level schedule (CSV) and ingress egress expectations; list any migration steps and expected minutes of warmup for KV cache.

Open questions / unknowns (action items):
- [ ] Confirm whether legal accepts soft-region burst for contracts with region pin as long as data flows remain in pinned region (we currently assume ephemeral compute outside region is OK for inference-only workloads). (Action: Janelle to sync with Legal, due 2027-08-10)
- [ ] Validate KV-cache restoration latency profiles across our proposed cross-region pairs - need microbenchmarks. (Action: Marco to run benchmark suite INF-bench-2027-08)
- [ ] Add traffic-class weighting: embeddings-heavy workloads may have different cost-profile vs chat/generation. Need to incorporate into SyncScore. (Action: Ravi to draft weighting update)

Quick checklist for Capacity Ops to run this planner for a renewal wave:
- Pull contracts CSV from billing (fields: contract_id, customer, committed_gpus, gpu_family, region_prefs, timezone, peak_window_local, soft_region_ok boolean, runway_months).
- Run normalization script -> hourly occupancy map per region (script: infra-planner/normalize_windows.py).
- Run sync-scorer (infra-planner/sync_score_v3) and export top-20 candidates.
- Create change bundles grouped by region and by ops-team owner; schedule maintenance windows for any baseline migration.
- Notify customers with proposed changes, include opt-out; implement only if accepted or if allowed by contract amendment.

Appendix: micro-sample CSV export format (planner output) - plain columns for ops automation:
contract_id,customer,region_assigned,committed_gpus,burst_eligible_hours_utc,burst_pool_id,sync_score,notes,last_update
C-4521,AtlasHealth,us-west1,24,"02:00-04:00",BP-7,62,"allow central overflow for 2 hours",2027-08-03
C-4789,FinBox,eu-west1,40,"13:00-17:00",BP-2,71,"shift 6 GPUs staggered",2027-08-03

Notes on risk tolerance and oversubscription:
- Default oversubscription cap for burst-eligible pools: 1.45x for non-critical workloads, 1.15x for critical latency-sensitive workloads.
- For multi-region pooled tranches set a hard cap that respects summed SLA guarantees across regions (we prefer conservative aggregation rather than optimistic).

Next steps (short-term):
- Finalize legal guidance (target 2027-08-10).
- Prototype a UI export for Console (product) showing "proposed sync benefits" per contract. (Owner: Product Console team, contact: Marco).
- Run a dry-run with Q3 renewal cohort (approx 34 contracts) by 2027-08-24 and measure realized utilization delta.

This doc is a working draft — expect churn. Use the linked artifacts for scripts and design PRs. If you copy text into Confluence, preserve the table samples and checklist for ops runbooks.

-- Aisha K.
